name: memwal
works_with: TypeScript apps, the Vercel AI SDK, and OpenClaw or NemoClaw through a plugin
short: Helps your agent add Walrus Memory to an app, so an AI agent keeps memory that carries across apps, sessions and workflows.
what: Walrus Memory is an SDK for agent memory. It stores memories on Walrus, encrypts them with SEAL, records ownership on the Sui blockchain and finds them again by meaning. The skill is a single-file reference covering installing, configuring, the API and troubleshooting, so your agent can wire it into your app.
who: Developers building agents in TypeScript who want memory that lives outside one app and that they control. The SKILL.md says it's not for throwaway chat context or large files. Walrus Memory is in beta.
needs: A delegate key and an account ID, generated at memory.walrus.xyz
Optional: `ai` and `zod` for the Vercel AI SDK integration

steps.title: Get your credentials
steps.text: Generate a delegate key and account ID at memory.walrus.xyz, or staging.memory.walrus.xyz for testing. Keep them in server environment variables.

steps.title: Give your agent the skill
steps.text: The README points agents to `SKILL.md` in the repo root as the full integration guide. Share it with your coding agent.

steps.title: Create a client
Or use it with OpenClaw
steps.text: Then add the plugin's config to `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` as the SKILL.md shows.

try.label: From the SKILL.md
try.text: Store a fact with `rememberAndWait("User prefers dark mode and works in TypeScript.")`, then call `recall({ query: "What are the user's preferences?" })`.

watch: Walrus Memory is in beta and still changing.
The delegate key is a private key. The SKILL.md says it belongs on the server only, never in browser code.
Your text goes to a relayer, which embeds, encrypts and uploads it. Use staging for prototypes and production for real data, and don't mix their credentials.
Forgetting a memory removes it from search, but the stored blob stays on Walrus until its storage period ends.
`remember()` always adds a new entry, so saving the same text twice gives two results. Recall has no relevance cutoff unless you set `maxDistance`.
